A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Mimic Score and Grad-Mimic. All 15 pages of v1 and 22 pages of v3, including their appendices, support comparison through readable text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original noisy-label classification experiments, DataComp/CLIP training and filtering results, dataset-quality analyses, and temperature studies in Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix D.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds comparator evaluations, runtime and memory measurements, clean-data selection experiments, and reference-model robustness studies in Appendices D–F.

M1.justification: Equation 2 and Algorithm 1 change softmax(-m/tau) to softmax(m/tau), correcting the specified weighting rule to favor higher Mimic Scores. This is a localized correction within the retained two-stage framework; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed. The new Stage 2 pseudocode documents the previously described selection and aggregation procedure.

E1.justification: The six image datasets and small/medium DataComp coverage, including its 38 downstream tasks, remain. Appendix E adds a clean-CIFAR100 subset-selection scenario without injected label noise, extending evaluation from identifying noisy samples to selecting useful examples among correctly labeled data.

E2.justification: V3 adds Rho-Loss comparisons in Tables 6–7 and an adapted validation-gradient influence comparator in Figure 6. Figure 8 adds random-subset comparisons for clean CIFAR100. Existing gradient and DataComp filtering baselines remain, while Table 1 removes the reference-model comparison rows.

E3.justification: New protocols include full-versus-hold-out reference training, validation sets with 1–20 examples per class, runtime and peak-memory measurements, and 50–80% clean subsets evaluated with ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14. Appendix C also replaces the five-epoch simulation description with 10 for DTD/Flowers102 and 5 for other datasets, called 'steps' in v3. This reported budget revision does not establish that retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained temperature and image/text encoder studies, v3 tests reference layers 7–11, Gaussian corruption of reference weights, references trained with less data, and sensitivity to validation-set size. New convergence and clean-subset analyses examine learning efficiency and utility beyond denoising. These substantially expand scrutiny of the method's dependencies and robustness.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose different initialization seeds for simulated reference models without specifying repeated-run counts. V3 introduces no new uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence-interval reporting, or significance testing; its additional experiments continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Retained method scores in Table 1 and the original DataComp and temperature results remain unchanged; v1 Tables 3 and 6 reappear in v3 Tables 8 and 9. V3 removes Table 1's reference-accuracy rows and adds substantial new results. Examples include average accuracy of 74.53 versus Rho-Loss's 73.77 at 50% label noise in Table 6 and a newly reported 20.7% reduction in DataComp training steps in Section 5.2.

T1.justification: V3 adds Appendix A's formal analysis, absent from v1: an L-smooth loss and noisy-gradient setup, three lemmas with proofs, and Theorem A.4. The theorem gives conditions involving reference-model error, temperature, gradient magnitude, and learning rate for improved one-step distance to the optimum relative to gradient descent.

C1.justification: The metric, automated filtering, and dataset-quality contributions remain, but computational efficiency and accelerated convergence become central scientific claims. The abstract newly claims 20.7% fewer CLIP training steps, and the conclusion adds a theoretical convergence contribution. The 4.7-million-sample reduction is promoted to the abstract from results already reported in v1.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations of computational savings relative to excess-loss and validation-gradient methods, interpretations of layer and reference-quality studies, and overshooting conditions from the theoretical analysis. The limitations move from Appendix A to G and change substantively: v1 suggests expert-designed filters for unreliable references, whereas v3 discusses bias/calibration risks and recommends checking the reference on a trusted benchmark.

D1.justification: Algorithm 2 newly specifies the decision matrix, Snorkel LabelModel operations, and a 0.5 retention-probability threshold. Conversely, Appendix C drops v1's exact image/text encoder parameter names. Core optimizer, learning-rate, batch-size, hardware, and pretrained-weight access information remain largely unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 substantially expands positioning against reference-loss and influence-based selection, adding discussion and citations for Rho-Loss, Rho-1, GREATS, LESS, ICONS, and classical influence functions. The introduction and related work reorganize the argument around model-free versus model-based selection and computational overhead, extending v1's positioning against noisy batch-gradient and specialized-filter approaches.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, and method exposition undergo extensive rewriting around efficiency and online/offline selection. Section headings and subsection organization change, the appendices expand and reorganize into A–G, and limitations move to the end. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: V3 shortens main-text Table 3 while preserving its full contents in Table 8, merges v1 Figures 5–6 into Figure 5, and adds a convergence panel to Figure 4. New comparison, efficiency, and robustness displays include Figures 6–9 and Tables 6–7 and 10–11. Table 1 loses its reference rows, and a glossary and second algorithm display are added.

improvement.justification: V3 resolves the reversed softmax specification and substantially strengthens assessment of the method through relevant model-based comparators, hold-out references, and explicit reference-quality tests. These address important weaknesses in v1's reliance on strong reference models and limited efficiency evidence. The conditional theory and Stage 2 pseudocode further improve transparency. Reporting weaknesses remain: Appendix C introduces steps/epochs ambiguity, and broad memory-saving claims exceed Figure 7's evidence, which shows 3968 MB for Grad-Mimic versus 3734 MB for Rho-Loss. Nevertheless, the corrected procedure and stronger comparative and robustness evidence provide a substantial overall improvement.
